candidates.title: GATE SHIFT
candidates.description: Tap a lane's gate to catch the glyph passing through it, correct only if its color matches that gate's currently assigned color, which reshuffles every few seconds.

candidates.title: SPARK CHAIN
candidates.description: Tap a charged node in a grid to ignite it, propagating to adjacent charged-enough nodes for a chained multiplier; timing and node choice decide chain length.

candidates.title: PULSE ECHO
candidates.description: The game flashes a growing sequence of glowing pads; tap pads back in the same order from memory to extend the streak, a wrong tap resets the sequence length.

candidates.title: FRONTIER CLAIM
candidates.description: Tap tiles to claim them before a hazard spreading from a source overtakes them; claimed tiles both score over time and block the hazard's path.

candidates.title: SLOT TRIAGE
candidates.description: Catch falling items into 3 limited inventory slots, then drag each to its matching output bin; capacity forces deciding what to keep versus discard.

candidates.title: DECAY VAULT
candidates.description: Stored items lose value over time unless spent holds reinforce them; deciding which items to protect with a limited reinforcement budget drives score.

candidates.title: SIGIL MATCH
candidates.description: Tap the set of cells matching a briefly shown glyph pattern among distractor cells before it changes to a new pattern elsewhere on the grid.

candidates.title: MOMENTUM FLING
candidates.description: Drag to fling an object with a direction and power set by the drag vector into differently scored zones based on entry angle.

candidates.title: BEACON RELAY
candidates.description: Hold a beacon to charge it, then relay that charge onward through a chain of beacons before it decays, choosing relay order and pacing.

reason: GATE SHIFT and PULSE ECHO tie on total, but GATE SHIFT's per-item routing decision under a periodically reshuffling rule is structurally unlike anything in works/ (C1/C3), while PULSE ECHO's memorize-and-reproduce sequence is a well-worn toy pattern; SPARK CHAIN scored highest on C7 but lower on C4/C5 since propagation timing is harder to teach in the first few taps.
